title: Implement the complete physical Gaussian tensor transform
body:
I connect the retained Gaussian expansion, complete chirp and principal-core compression into a physical source-box transform. The isolated `research/physical-gaussian-tensor/` package includes actual coefficient production, four canonical full-support gathers/scatters, short-field moves, periodic halos, original-axis page reuse, source-core assembly and exact normalization restoration.

Under the stated production and inherited transfer contracts, I derive the `R F_s` error bound with `D=d-1` and `gamma=D(2u+ceilLog2(32p)+1)`. I charge the catalogue, spectators, metadata, numerical children and polynomial setup, retaining the existing `.99827619697` transfer allowance. I state the caller growth laws and leave the selected frontier unchanged.

I check the explicit p48/P80 fixture against separate natural-coordinate staged references: 49 inputs, 64 middle coordinates and 49 outputs, with 4,900 final bits and 12 nonzero restored outputs in each direction. The producer regenerates all 113,537 coefficient cells before the consumers use its authenticated immutable return. I also check altered-axis and half-disk rejection, positive reuse, protected outputs and fixed scratch restoration.

I preserve precision and fixtures while using fixed digits, streamed division, one-pass accumulators, saturating leaf admission and direct bounded signed records. I check literal two's-complement bits, wider-width and physical-alias fallbacks, malformed-input error order and partial-output cleanup. I preload the numerical import cohort and restore its direct and copied helper bindings after each scope. I retain the exact numerical formulas and fixed tape bounds. `ARITHMETIC.md` gives the proofs and ownership checks; `CATALOGUE.md` records the page's provenance.

At `f687fa171ef760fa98a4be1289717b47dd4ee0b3`, I passed metadata, the 57-file publication check and source-history validation. I passed all six commands from the official Git-free export and checked unchanged bytes and modes for its 58 files, including the receipt. Stage times: 2.863, 4.843, 33.144, 120.529, 142.613 and 143.197 seconds. The declared limits total 1,200 seconds, with a 390-second maximum. Export SHA256: `6b977956b2794094de4aa50545baceff9e43ccc68a473ce5569e6a710b97bac0`; receipt SHA256: `115580f6c53a84c7e09401095e8ea7d043406adcd50cc5cf34d0b3e9d0a162aa`.

I matched all six successful [hosted replay](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39402389419) records to that export and checked the successful unchanged-input step. The hosted numerical replay ran from 09:44:08 to 10:02:12 UTC on October 20. I verified test merge `c8c304f4cfd181007bfc0bd9ff83a35fda960b9e` against the published tree. I merged current main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244` after reading priority revision 7, then refreshed that same main before this handoff; all 15 live scientific inputs and the original historical provenance remain unchanged. In [Discussion3664](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664), I retain earlier timeouts, the interrupted attempt, exact receipts and overlap checks.

I use the finite witness for staged conformance, outside the production precision, separation and locality domain, with reduced Gaussian halos and retained q2 literal children. Its repeated 7×7 source lengths do not form a pairwise-coprime CRT witness. I leave production-sized execution, inherited universal supplier premises, numerical composition with CRT/integer recovery and independent human or formal-kernel review open. Tekalign's complementary [PR4024](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4024) supplies the separate encoded address conversion.

Jose Manuel (`jmbarrancoml`), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. I retain the complete source exports and attribution from PR3878/3851/3787/3763/3709/3640, Dugongue's PR3877, the RaD project/hipotures and the nested source notices. The package records predecessor credit and the scope of adjacent contributions.
